name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Brad Schneider running with large financial advantage ($3.0M raised, $1.7M on hand)
Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht has no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: The seat's D+12 partisan lean, Schneider's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and a challenger with no visible resources all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets agree at roughly 96%. With no polls available, uncertainty stays moderate but the fundamentals leave little doubt.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Schneider or an unusually strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider seeks another term in this northern Illinois district, which leans Democratic by about twelve points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.7 million on hand after raising over $3 million, while Republican Carl Lambrecht reports no fundraising and draws no outside support. Prediction markets give Schneider about a 96% chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. Everything points to a safe Democratic hold, with the main open question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
